title: Input-chunk metadata scalar queries reach unconstrained logging callbacks
why: flb_input_chunk_has_direct_routes and flb_input_chunk_get_event_type call cio_meta_read; the file path can enter mmap_file, whose diagnostic path invokes cio->options.log_cb. The callback has no bounded custody or counted-user effect in the selected contract vocabulary. A metadata-view helper also publishes borrowed interior pointers via an out parameter. These two queries stay undeclared. Discharge by a checked callback effect and view-lifetime reading, then remeasure the corpus and system slice.

title: Input-chunk output-size accounting wrappers reach configurable log callbacks
why: flb_input_chunk_output_size_subtract and flb_input_chunk_update_output_instances conditionally log; the logging path can update counters and invoke a configured metrics log callback. Without a checked bound on its custody and counted-user effects, neither wrapper gets an unconditional neutral contract. Discharge by constraining the callback path or a guarded contract with audited semantics, then remeasure.

title: Raw output-thread TLS getter returns retained storage
why: flb_output_thread_instance_get returns a thread-local pointer that aliases retained storage, like pthread_getspecific. Resource-v1 return_none cannot express that relation. It stays undeclared even though the scalar flb_output_flush_id_get wrapper can be stated as a borrowed/neutral caller effect. Discharge with a retained-result relation and matching Lean parity or a recorded refusal.

title: Flush create, destroy, finished and dispatch effects remain unmodeled
why: Flush create/destroy/finished/dispatch can retain or release flush/task resources and run callbacks; this card's ID helper contract does not state their effects or imply lifecycle safety. Preserve the existing OR-1/OR-7 defining-body refutations (provisional Unsafe) and their Unknown callers. Discharge this residual only by stating and checking the still-unstated lifecycle effects with Rust controls and matching Lean parity; adding those contracts does not require overturning valid refutations.
